ledger.claim: POL-RD-01's gate is passed on this trip's own measurement. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 29.98 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 24.0 km, an excess of 5.98 km — 24.9% of optimal. Both limbs of the establishment test are therefore satisfied: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The governing figure is the trace figure; POL-RD-01 expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for this test, so the rounded 30.0 km is not relied on here.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged and the burden has shifted to the driver. The artifacts describe one trip — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry TRP-00111 — and the excess is measured from a trace that is not impaired on any of the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) tests: 229 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s. Under POL-RD-08 the driver must now make out a named clause against a named artifact; naming the clause is not the same as satisfying it.

POL-RD-03 is not made out on this record, because both of its route limbs depend on knowing the path of the OPTIMAL route and that path is absent. Limb (a) requires an advisory naming a road or segment 'that the optimal route traverses'; limb (c) requires an actual route that leaves that corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. Trip_record.optimal_route_source is prose only ('optimal is BKE southbound then PIE westbound, no gantry at this hour'), and the derived advisory_area block states in terms that 'the optimal route's own polyline is not in the record'. The only test the package ran was whether the driver's own trace entered the advisory's bounding box (trace_enters_area true, 12 fixes inside, minimum_distance_m 0.0) — and that test is confounded, because the trace is inside that box precisely by virtue of the diversion that is the conduct complained of. A diverted trace's presence in the closure area cannot show that the optimal route traverses the closed sub-segment, and the derived block itself says it 'decides nothing by itself'. The exoneration therefore fails at its first limb and POL-RD-03 is unavailable.

Alternatively, if the tribunal treats the corridor match as decided by the assessor's narration rather than by a computed fact, limb (c) is still unverified: the record's only statement about the rejoin is the note that the trace shows 'the rejoin on the AYE', and no derived fact in the package tests whether that rejoin put the vehicle back on the optimal corridor before the dropoff. On a record that cannot show the optimal corridor at all, the 'matched by an actual route' limb cannot be run.

No distance may be excluded as rider-requested, so the excess stands as measured. The chat log shows the DRIVER announcing the diversion ('boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok') and the rider replying only 'as long as i reach by 8.30'. There is no instruction from the rider at all, so POL-RD-04(a) fails; and nothing in the rider's reply identifies a place or road specifically enough to act on, so POL-RD-04(c) fails. chat_message.waypoint_hint is null on both messages, and POL-RD-04 makes that field the only permitted source for the 200 m corroboration test, so that test cannot be run either and the clause is unavailable.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, computed against the booked optimal route because no exculpatory clause excuses any part of the excess, and the ruling must state its lines separately. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = 31.00. charged_total = 37.74. Refund = 37.74 - 31.00 = 6.74, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 6.75, which is 17.9% of charged_total — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% FULL_REFUND share. The surge multiplier read for this computation is 1.0, taken from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which POL-RD-02 makes the only source for it. The contested amount is 8.00, so the correct remedy is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.75 and the rider should not be left carrying that distance-and-time overcharge.

No pass-through line changes the figure in either direction, so the refund is not overstated. fare_breakdown.tolls_erp is 0.00 and erp_gantries is empty, optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, there is no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), and waiting_time_fee and promo_discount are both 0.00. Under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and could never be added on top of it; here there is none to comprehend, so the rider's recovery is confined to the distance-and-time overcharge.

Pleaded in the alternative only, and only if the tribunal holds the record genuinely silent — rather than merely unhelpful — on whether the closed PIE segment lies on the optimal route. The driver invokes POL-RD-03 against an artifact that does not carry the route geometry the clause's own test needs, and the record holds no field from which that geometry can be read; on that reading POL-RD-10(5) applies. The outcome is then ESCALATE, which is terminal: no monetary outcome issues and the disputed amount is HELD rather than collected. That is the least the rider should get where the platform's own routing record cannot answer the question the driver's defence turns on.

Measured as POL-RD-01 requires, the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 29.98 km against a booked optimal of 24.0 km — an excess of 5.98 km and 24.9%, over both the 0.8 km absolute gate and the 20% proportional gate, and I do not dispute that a deviation is ESTABLISHED on the trace. Note that the trip_record's 30.0 km is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for this test. Establishment is not the end of the enquiry: the whole of that excess is attributable to an LTA closure and is exonerated by POL-RD-03 in the claims that follow.

The external cause is on the record as a real, admitted artifact, not as an assertion. EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is an LTA DataMall advisory, type CLOSURE, severity HIGH, for the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit' — the very corridor the booked optimal route traverses (routing-engine-v3.2: BKE southbound then PIE westbound) — active from 07:10 to 09:30 on the trip date, a validity window that brackets the whole trip from 07:47:40 to 08:25:40 with buffer at both ends, and the artifact records intersects_route true and overlaps_trip_window true. POL-RD-03 limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied on this artifact alone.

Limb (c) is satisfied on the trip's own trace and on the parties' statements. The telemetry is unbroken 10-second sampling with 100% coverage, and the derived advisory-area test on that trace puts 12 fixes inside the advisory's geometry with a minimum distance of 0.0 m and trace_enters_area true, while the admissibility note records the exit at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and the rejoin on the AYE after it — which is precisely the leave-before-and-rejoin-after pattern limb (c) demands, and matches the advisory's own diversion instruction 'via Upper Bukit Timah Rd'. The driver said the same thing to the rider in the chat at 07:54:20: 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok'.

The exoneration cap does not bite on this route. The justified excess is min(measured 5.98 km, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 29.2 km - booked optimal 24.0 km) + 1.00 km) = min(5.98, 1.30 x 5.2 + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The cap of 7.76 km is larger than the measured excess of 5.98 km, so the WHOLE of the excess is exonerated and no residuum survives for a POL-RD-02 distance refund.

Even if POL-RD-02 is run against the closure-adjusted optimal route that POL-RD-03 prescribes — 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km with the booked 30.0 minute optimal scaled by 29.98/24.0 to 37.5 minutes — the arithmetic gives (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x the surge_multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 37.585, against a charged_total of 37.74. The difference is 0.155, far below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so even on the branch least favourable to the driver the outcome is NO_ACTION and the charged fare stands.

There is nothing for POL-RD-09 to correct on this trip. erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00; the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00. The re-route down Upper Bukit Timah and around by the AYE crossed no gantry at this hour, and no surcharge line appears in the fare_breakdown at all. No pass-through refund is due, and no billing-integrity defect exists for the rider to take under POL-RD-09(4).

The trace is clean at policy level and the case is fit for a final ruling. It carries 229 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval against an expected 10 seconds, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it does not meet any of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) and needs no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii). Nor does any POL-RD-10 trigger fire: the trip identifiers match across EV-TRIP-00111, EV-GPS-00111 and EV-FARE-00111; the timestamps run forwards and are consistent; the refund in issue (0.155) is nowhere near the SGD 150.00 ceiling or charged_total; and every charge line has its counterpart in the record.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be run against this driver on the clause's own fields. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 588 — nowhere near POL-RD-06's three-flag test or its 5% test. The point is academic in any event because a deviation is additionally MATERIAL only above 50% or 8.0 km, and this one is 24.9% and 5.98 km, so the POL-RD-06 profile check is not even engaged on this trip. POL-RD-06 can neither uplift the remedy against this driver nor generate a conduct referral.

The shifted burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged exactly as that clause requires: the driver points to a specific artifact, the LTA closure advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01, and a specific clause, POL-RD-03. The rider's contrary assertion — 'I did not see any closure' — cites no evidence ID at all and by POL-RD-08 carries no weight. The rider's profile supplies no factor either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's four-claim corroboration trigger is not met. This case is decided on the trip's own trace, advisory and fare record, and on those artifacts the rider's $8.00 claim is not supported.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. This is decided on the trip's own records, TRP-00111.

1. The distance. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00111 records 29.98 km travelled against a booked optimal of 24.0 km on EV-TRIP-00111: an excess of 5.98 km, or 24.9% of optimal. That passes both of POL-RD-01's gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. Both advocates agree on this and I accept it, using the trace figure as POL-RD-01 requires (the trip record's rounded 30.0 km is not used for the test).

2. The closure. The bundle carries a real LTA record, EV-ADVIS-00111-01: a HIGH-severity closure of the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Clementi Rd exit (between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit), in force 07:10–09:30 on 3 Aug 2026, overlapping the whole trip (07:47:40–08:25:40), with the diversion stated as Upper Bukit Timah Rd. The booked optimal route is 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound' (EV-TRIP-00111, optimal_route_source), so the advisory names the expressway and the segment the optimal route uses; the trace leaves that corridor at Bukit Panjang before the closed segment and rejoins it on the AYE after it. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met and the deviation is EXONERATED.

3. The cap. POL-RD-03 exonerates at most min(measured 5.98 km, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.00) = min(5.98, 7.76) = 5.98 km. The cap does not bite, so the whole excess is justified and nothing is left over as a refundable overcharge.

4. The fare. Even running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal (24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km, duration 30.0 x 29.98/24.0 = 37.5 min), the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 37.585, against charged_total 37.74. The difference is 0.155, which is below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis threshold, so no refundable amount remains and the charge stands.

5. The rider's objections, answered together. I reject the argument that POL-RD-03 cannot be run because the optimal route's polyline is absent from the record: the clause asks whether the advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, and the booked optimal route's own source names PIE westbound - the corridor the advisory closes. The derived trace-area figure was one input, not the whole basis. The rider's statement 'I did not see any closure' cites no evidence ID and carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The rider's pleaded alternative, that POL-RD-10(5) should escalate because the driver's clause lacks the field it needs, fails: the advisory is in the pool, covers the trip window, and carries the road, window and geometry the clause requires, so no POL-RD-10(5) trigger fires.

6. The other clauses. No distance is excluded as rider-requested under POL-RD-04: the chat log's only rider message ('as long as i reach by 8.30') is not an instruction, and waypoint_hint is null, so the clause is unavailable. Nothing is refundable under POL-RD-09: tolls_erp is 0.00, erp_gantries is empty, and no ERP or surcharge line exists to correct (POL-RD-09(2) has nothing to pass through). No driver compensation is due under POL-RD-04: the billed distance is 30.0 km, which is not less than the 29.98 km travelled.

7. No escalation and no referral. The trace is clean at policy level (229 fixes, 10 s sampling, no gaps, 100% coverage), the trip identifiers and timestamps match across the trip record, trace and fare record, every charge line reconciles, and the driver's defence rests on a present advisory that covers the trip window - so no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. No repeat-deviation pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d 0 of 588 trips), the deviation is not material (24.9% and 5.98 km, under the 50%/8.0 km test), and there is no billing-integrity defect, so no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral and no POL-RD-09(4) billing referral is made. All evidence used here carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so no discount or narration under POL-GEN-02 applies.

Outcome: NO_ACTION - the rider's claim is not supported on the evidence and the charged fare of SGD 37.74 stands. The monetary effect is zero, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. Earlier cases P-0001 and P-0002 (POL-RD-01/02/08) ended in partial refunds; the difference here is the live LTA closure advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 matching the optimal corridor and the trip window, which exonerated the whole of the excess.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
